title: TN Visa RSU Tax Rate: US vs Canada Complete Comparison 2026
description: Compare RSU tax rates for TN visa holders in the US vs Canada. Discover which country offers better net pay, how to optimize withholding, and reduce your tax burden legally.
content:
## Key Takeaways

- **US RSU taxes:** 22-37% federal + 0-13.3% state = **22-50% total**
- **Canada RSU taxes:** 20.5-33% federal + 5-21% provincial = **26-54% total**
- TN visa holders can save **$12,000-$25,000** annually by working in lower-tax US states
- Tax treaty benefits don't reduce rates but prevent double taxation
- Use our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator) to compare your exact net pay

## TN Visa RSU Taxation: US vs Canada Side-by-Side

### How the US Taxes RSUs (TN Visa Holders)

When your RSUs vest while you're on TN status working in the US:

**Federal Income Tax:**
- Supplemental wage withholding: **22% flat rate** (up to $1M)
- For vesting >$1M/year: **37% flat rate**
- Your actual tax rate depends on total income (see marginal rates below)

**Social Security + Medicare (FICA):**
- 6.2% Social Security (up to $168,600 wage base in 2026)
- 1.45% Medicare (no limit)
- 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax if income >$200K single/$250K married
- **Total FICA: 7.65%** (or 8.55% for high earners)

**State Income Tax:**
- **California:** 9.3-13.3% (highest in US)
- **New York:** 4-10.9%
- **Massachusetts:** 5%
- **Texas/Florida/Washington:** 0% (no state tax)

**Example: $100K RSU vesting in California**
- Federal: $22,000
- FICA: $7,650
- California: $9,300
- **Total withholding: $38,950** (39%)
- **Net proceeds: $61,050**

### How Canada Taxes RSUs (Residents)

When your RSUs vest while you're a Canadian tax resident:

**Federal Income Tax (2026 rates):**
- $55,867 or less: 15%
- $55,868-$111,733: 20.5%
- $111,734-$173,205: 26%
- $173,206-$246,752: 29%
- Over $246,752: **33%**

**Provincial Income Tax (Ontario example):**
- $51,446 or less: 5.05%
- $51,447-$102,894: 9.15%
- $102,895-$150,000: 11.16%
- $150,001-$220,000: 12.16%
- Over $220,000: **13.16%**

**CPP/EI Contributions:**
- CPP: 5.95% (max $3,867 in 2026)
- EI: 1.58% (max $1,049 in 2026)
- **Total: ~7.5%** (but capped, unlike FICA)

**Example: $100K RSU vesting in Ontario**
- Federal tax: $26,000 (26% marginal rate)
- Ontario tax: $11,160 (11.16%)
- CPP/EI: $3,867 (capped)
- **Total: $41,027** (41%)
- **Net proceeds: $58,973**

**Comparison:**
- US (California): $61,050 net (39% tax)
- Canada (Ontario): $58,973 net (41% tax)
- **Difference: $2,077 more in US** (3.4% higher net pay)

## Marginal vs Effective Tax Rates: What Actually Matters

### Example: TN Visa Holder at Meta ($180K salary + $200K RSU)

**US (California):**
- Total income: $380,000
- Marginal rate: 35% federal + 13.3% CA = **48.3%**
- Effective rate: **34.2%** (after deductions)
- Total tax: $129,960
- **Net pay: $250,040**

**Canada (Ontario):**
- Total income: $380,000 CAD (~$280K USD at 1.36 FX)
- Marginal rate: 29% federal + 13.16% ON = **42.16%**
- Effective rate: **32.8%**
- Total tax: $124,640 CAD ($91,647 USD)
- **Net pay: $188,353 USD**

**Winner: US by $61,687** (24.6% higher net pay)

**Why the difference?**
1. USD vs CAD exchange rate (1.36x purchasing power)
2. Higher US tech salaries (Canada pays 20-30% less)
3. Lower US tax rates at high income levels

**1. Washington (Seattle/Redmond)**
- State tax: **0%**
- Federal + FICA: 29.65%
- **Total effective: ~30%**
- **Net on $100K RSU: $70,350**
- Employers: Amazon, Microsoft, Meta (remote)

**2. Texas (Austin)**
- State tax: **0%**
- Federal + FICA: 29.65%
- **Total effective: ~30%**
- **Net on $100K RSU: $70,350**
- Employers: Tesla, Oracle, Apple

**3. Florida (Miami)**
- State tax: **0%**
- Federal + FICA: 29.65%
- **Total effective: ~30%**
- **Net on $100K RSU: $70,350**
- Employers: Citadel, hedge funds, remote tech

### Worst States for TN Visa Holders (Highest RSU Tax)

**1. California (SF Bay Area)**

- Federal + FICA: 29.65%
- **Total effective: ~43%**
- **Net on $100K RSU: $57,000**

**2. New York (NYC)**
- State tax: 10.9% + NYC 3.876%

- **Total effective: ~44.4%**

**3. New Jersey**
- State tax: 10.75%

- **Total effective: ~40.4%**
- **Net on $100K RSU: $59,600**

## The TN Visa Tax Optimization Strategy

### Scenario 1: You're Choosing Where to Work

If you have job offers in multiple locations:

**Offer A: Google Mountain View, CA**
- Salary: $200K
- RSU: $300K/year
- Total: $500K
- Tax: ~43% = $215,000
- **Net: $285,000**

**Offer B: Amazon Seattle, WA**
- Salary: $190K (5% less)
- RSU: $280K/year (7% less)
- Total: $470K (6% less gross)
- Tax: ~30% = $141,000
- **Net: $329,000**
- **Winner: Seattle by $44,000** (15% more net despite lower gross)

**Pro Tip:** When negotiating, always calculate **net** compensation, not gross. A 10% lower offer in a zero-tax state often beats a higher offer in California.

### Scenario 2: You're Returning to Canada

If you're moving back to Canada, which province minimizes your tax?

**Assumptions:**
- Remote tech job: $120K CAD salary
- Unvested US RSUs: $80K USD/year
- Total: ~$200K CAD

**Option A: Stay in Ontario**
- Tax: 42% = $84,000 CAD
- **Net: $116,000 CAD**

**Option B: Move to Alberta**
- Tax: 39% = $78,000 CAD
- **Net: $122,000 CAD**
- **Savings: $6,000/year**

**Option C: Move to BC (Vancouver)**
- Tax: 45.5% = $91,000 CAD
- **Net: $109,000 CAD**
- **Loss vs Alberta: $13,000/year**

### Scenario 3: You're Commuting Cross-Border (Detroit ↔ Windsor)

Some TN visa holders live in Canada and work in the US. How does taxation work?

**Tax treatment:**
- US taxes your W-2 wages (you work in US)
- Canada taxes your worldwide income (you're a resident)
- You claim Foreign Tax Credit in Canada for US tax paid

**Example: Work in Detroit, live in Windsor**
- Salary: $150K USD
- RSU: $100K USD
- US tax: 35% = $87,500
- Canada tax: 42% on $250K CAD = $105,000 CAD
- Foreign Tax Credit: $87,500 USD = $119,000 CAD
- **Net Canada tax owed: $0** (FTC exceeds Canada tax)
- **Winner: You get a refund!**

**But watch out:**
- Michigan has 4.25% state tax (not covered by treaty)
- Ontario won't credit Michigan tax (only federal)
- Net result: You pay **both** federal US + Ontario tax

## Withholding Optimization: How to Keep More Money Now

### Problem: Automatic 22% Withholding Doesn't Match Your Rate

If your actual tax rate is 35%, the 22% withholding leaves you **underwithheld**. You'll owe $13,000 at tax time on $100K vesting.

### Solution 1: Adjust W-4 for Extra Withholding

**Step 1:** Calculate your expected tax shortfall
- Total income: $300K
- RSU vesting: $150K
- Withholding: $33K (22%)
- Actual tax: $52.5K (35%)
- **Shortfall: $19.5K**

**Step 2:** Update W-4 Line 4(c)
- Divide shortfall by pay periods: $19,500 / 24 = $812.50
- Enter "$813" on W-4 Line 4(c) (extra withholding per paycheck)

**Result:** No surprise tax bill in April

### Solution 2: Make Quarterly Estimated Payments

**When to use:** If you have large RSU vestings ($500K+)

**Deadlines:**
- Q1: April 15
- Q2: June 15
- Q3: September 15
- Q4: January 15 (next year)

**How much to pay:** 110% of last year's tax (safe harbor) or 90% of current year's estimated tax

**Pro Tip:** Use [IRS Form 1040-ES](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-1040-es) worksheet

### Solution 3: Sell Shares to Cover Tax (Stock-for-Tax)

Most equity platforms (E*TRADE, Fidelity) offer "sell-to-cover" at vesting:

- RSU vests: 100 shares @ $100 = $10,000
- Withholding needed: $2,200 (22%)
- Platform auto-sells: 22 shares
- **You receive: 78 shares** ($7,800 value)

**Pros:**
- Automatic (no action needed)
- Covers withholding exactly
- No out-of-pocket cash required

**Cons:**
- You're selling at vesting price (might be low)
- Locks in current stock price

## Real Example: TN Visa Software Engineer at Stripe

**Profile:**
- Juan, Mexican citizen on TN visa
- Senior SWE at Stripe San Francisco
- $180K salary + $220K/year RSU
- Total comp: $400K

**Current situation (California):**
- Federal tax: $92,000 (28%)
- California tax: $46,000 (11.5%)
- FICA: $13,800
- **Total tax: $151,800** (38%)
- **Net pay: $248,200**

**Option A: Transfer to Stripe Seattle office**
- Same salary: $180K
- Same RSU: $220K
- Total: $400K
- Federal + FICA: $105,800
- Washington state: $0
- **Total tax: $105,800** (26.5%)
- **Net pay: $294,200**
- **Savings: $46,000/year** (18.5% increase in take-home)

**Option B: Return to Mexico (remote work)**
- Mexican tax rate: 30% (resident)
- US withholding: 30% (non-resident)
- Tax treaty: Allows credit for US tax in Mexico
- **Net tax: ~30%** (similar to US)
- **But:** Cost of living in Mexico City is 60% lower
- **Result: Effective 3x purchasing power boost**

## Tax Treaty Benefits for TN Visa Holders

The US-Mexico and US-Canada tax treaties provide:

### 1. No Double Taxation on Wages

**Article XV:** Employment income is taxed where you work, not where you're a citizen.

**Example:**
- Canadian citizen on TN visa working in Texas
- US taxes your salary (you work in US)
- Canada doesn't tax it (treaty exemption)
- **Result: Only US tax applies**

**But:** If you keep Canadian residency (spouse/kids in Canada), you're taxed in Canada with FTC for US tax paid.

### 2. Reduced Withholding on Dividends/Interest

**Article X:** US withholds only 15% on dividends paid to treaty residents (vs 30% for non-treaty)

**Example:**
- You hold $100K in US stocks
- Dividends: $2,000/year
- Withholding: $300 (15%) vs $600 (30%)
- **Savings: $300/year**

### 3. Exemption for Stock Options (ISOs)

**Article XV:** Stock option income is allocated based on work period, just like RSUs.

**Example:**
- 4-year ISO grant while on TN visa
- You exercise after returning to Canada
- US taxes gain attributable to US work period
- Canada taxes gain attributable to Canadian period

## When Should You Move Back to Canada?

**From a pure tax perspective:**

**Stay in US if:**
- You work in WA/TX/FL (0% state tax)
- Your income >$200K (US rates more favorable)
- You plan to stay long-term (401k, Social Security benefits)

**Return to Canada if:**
- You value universal healthcare (US insurance costs $500-$1,500/month)
- You want to buy property (Canada has better mortgage rates)
- You have family ties (quality of life > tax savings)
- You're earning <$150K (Canada's benefits outweigh tax difference)

**Pro Tip:** Run the numbers with our [calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator) before deciding.

## Action Checklist

**Before accepting a TN visa job offer:**
- [ ] Calculate net pay (not gross) using our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator)
- [ ] Compare state tax rates (prioritize WA/TX/FL if possible)
- [ ] Factor in cost of living (California housing costs offset higher pay)
- [ ] Negotiate RSU refresh grants (ongoing equity matters more than initial grant)

**During TN employment:**
- [ ] Adjust W-4 withholding if you're under/over-withheld
- [ ] Make quarterly estimated payments if vesting >$100K/year
- [ ] Track days in US vs Canada (for residency determination)
- [ ] Set aside 40-50% of RSU vesting for taxes (don't spend it all!)

**When returning to Canada:**
- [ ] Calculate work period attribution for unvested RSUs
- [ ] File dual-country returns with Foreign Tax Credit claim
- [ ] Consider accelerated vesting to avoid multi-year filings
- [ ] Consult cross-border CPA if total RSU >$300K
